content_voiceover: Here's the pivotal trial that established venetoclax plus azacitidine as standard of care for older, unfit AML patients, the VIALE-A trial. Four hundred thirty-one patients with newly diagnosed AML who were unfit for intensive induction, median age seventy-six, were randomized two to one to either azacitidine plus venetoclax at four hundred milligrams, or azacitidine plus placebo. The survival curves separate early and stay separated, median overall survival was fourteen point seven months with the combination versus just nine point six months with azacitidine alone, a highly significant difference with a hazard ratio of zero point six six. Response rates tell the same story, complete remission was thirty-six point seven percent versus seventeen point nine percent, and if you include CR with incomplete count recovery, the combined response rate jumps to sixty-six point four percent versus twenty-eight point three percent. This trial is why venetoclax-azacitidine is now the default backbone for unfit AML patients everywhere, and it's a very testable trial, know the name VIALE-A, the population, and those survival numbers.
keypoints: VIALE-A, four hundred thirty-one unfit AML patients, median age seventy-six
Azacitidine plus venetoclax versus azacitidine plus placebo, two to one randomization
Median overall survival, fourteen point seven months versus nine point six months
Complete remission rate, thirty-six point seven percent versus seventeen point nine percent
Hazard ratio zero point six six, p less than zero point zero zero one
keypoint_voiceover: Memorize VIALE-A as azacitidine plus venetoclax in unfit AML, with a median overall survival benefit of about five months, fourteen point seven versus nine point six, and roughly double the complete remission rate compared to azacitidine alone.
